papers.venue: IEEE iCONEECT 2026 · Premier University, Chittagong · 25–26 Sep 2026
papers.title: FUZZLE: A Hybrid Fuzzy Ensemble Machine Learning Framework for Interpretable Alzheimer’s Disease Staging Using OASIS Dataset
papers.authors: **Nafees Al Mahadi**, Fairose Chahara Tohfa, Syed Khairul Islam, Amena Afrin Alo, Al Mamun Samrat, Sizan Md Thowhidul Islam
papers.summary: A Sugeno-type neuro-fuzzy system with 12 expert-defined rules, fused with a cross-validated weighted ensemble over 26 engineered clinical and MRI-derived features. A strict patient-level split prevents leakage. SHAP and the fired fuzzy rules explain every prediction in a prototype clinical decision support system.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative condition that remains challenging to stage accurately and in a timely manner, while maintaining both prediction accuracy and clinical interpretability. This study proposes FUZZLE, combining ensemble learning with a fuzzy inference system for transparent AD staging on the OASIS longitudinal dataset. Twenty-six discriminative features were engineered from clinical variables and neuroimaging data. The Sugeno-type neuro-fuzzy system has 12 expert-defined linguistic rules; class-balanced learning addresses imbalance, and the final prediction comes from a cross-validation based weighted ensemble optimized via grid search. With a strict patient-level split (120 training / 30 testing patients), the hybrid model achieved 79.45% accuracy and a macro F1-score of 0.7325, improving on the best standalone model (Extra Trees, 73.97%) and the independent neuro-fuzzy model (71.23%). SHAP analysis identified MMSE, nWBV and the Age×MMSE interaction as the most significant variables, consistent with the expert fuzzy knowledge base.

papers.venue: IEEE COMPAS 2026 · University of Dhaka · 9–10 Oct 2026
papers.title: A Weighted Soft-Voting Ensemble for Nowcasting Pedestrian Evacuation Route Status
papers.authors: Amena Afrin Alo, **Nafees Al Mahadi**, Snaholata Mondal
papers.summary: A full pipeline that turns 24 million raw, unlabeled pedestrian trajectories from Czech train stations into a crowd-safety classifier (Optimal, Congested or Dangerous). It uses 2 m grid cells per 10-second window and a leakage audit (average speed alone gave 91%, so it was removed), then combines five tree models and a linear learner by weighted soft voting.
papers.abstract: Crowd crush at train stations is a major safety problem, and most systems only detect it after it happens. This study builds a full machine learning pipeline that tells if a walking path is OPTIMAL, CONGESTED or DANGEROUS, using a dataset of 24 million pedestrian records from two Czech train stations. With no labels or ready features, the study builds a new labeling method and cleaning process: raw positions become 2 m × 2 m grid boxes checked every 10 seconds (nowcasting). Leaking features were removed. Six baselines (Random Forest, XGBoost, CatBoost, Extra Trees, Decision Tree, Naive Bayes) are compared with a Hybrid Ensemble using weighted soft voting. On 168,639 unseen test samples the ensemble reaches 97.15% accuracy, F1 0.9716 and MCC 0.9573 at the best seed, with mean F1 0.9712 (±0.0003) over ten seeds. Of 57,027 truly dangerous samples, only 21 are wrongly called safe.
